q: Who decides what is memorable: an upstream agent/user, or a memory-owned extractor?
a: Engram answers “the agent,” with optional prompt/passive capture; persistence accepts already-curated observations (docs/codebase/memory-core.md:7-23).

q: Should raw user input be retained alongside curated memory?
a: Engram stores user prompts as first-class retrievable records and can auto-capture the current prompt during save (internal/store/store.go:261-274; internal/mcp/mcp.go:1421-1430).

q: What privacy mechanism is enforceable: delimited redaction, semantic exclusion, or source separation?
a: Engram strips literal ...

q: Must memory writes be complete, or may partial records enter and be repaired later?
a: Engram now rejects blank post-redaction titles and content because a poison mutation blocks the ordered project queue (internal/store/store.go:2898-2929).

q: Is a memory a typed document, a normalized claim graph, or an event/evidence structure?
a: Engram chooses a typed free-text document with metadata (internal/store/store.go:118-137).

q: Should changing knowledge update one stable topic, append a new claim, or create an explicit supersession edge?
a: A non-empty topic_key updates the most recently updated matching project/scope row in place and increments revision_count; distinct untitled saves append (internal/store/store.go:2946-2990).

q: Are scopes ownership/security boundaries or retrieval conveniences?
a: Engram stores project, personal, and global; project is the default, personal crosses projects when no override is supplied, and relations reject cross-project pairs (docs/codebase/memory-core.md:43-49; internal/mcp/mcp.go:1123-1129

q: Should the local database or cloud be authoritative?
a: Engram chooses local SQLite; cloud is opt-in replication and shared access (docs/codebase/mental-model.md:5-16).

q: What counts as a duplicate: same semantic claim, same normalized body, same topic, or same external identity?
a: Engram uses three answers: exact normalized content plus project/scope/type/title within 15 minutes increments duplicate_count; equal topic_key revises a row; import dedupes by portable sync_id (internal/store/store.go:2931-3038

q: Does a conflict block the write, annotate it, or get resolved before persistence?
a: Engram commits the memory first, then runs non-fatal candidate detection; candidate failure never fails save (internal/mcp/mcp.go:1408-1419,1449-1466).

q: Who judges semantic relationships: deterministic code, an LLM, or a human?
a: Engram uses lexical FTS to propose candidates, then accepts agent/human-like mem_judge or optional semantic runner verdicts with actor/model/evidence/confidence provenance (internal/store/relations.go:73-100,736-759).

q: Should “not a conflict” be remembered?
a: Engram persists not_conflict as a real verdict so the same pair is suppressed later (internal/store/relations.go:32-59,352-355).

q: Should retrieval be lexical, vector, structured, or hybrid?
a: Engram uses trigram FTS5 plus LIKE for short terms, with weighted BM25 and optional all|any token semantics (internal/store/store.go:4162-4172,4246-4269).

q: How are results ordered?
a: Search orders by BM25 rank; title weight is 5, content 1, topic key 3, other indexed fields 0 (internal/store/store.go:4246-4269).

q: How much content should a first retrieval expose?
a: Engram returns bounded previews, with full content obtained separately; preview content is explicitly excluded from the struct and SQL truncates to 300 characters (internal/store/store.go:168-170; internal/store/store.go:4240-4243).

q: Does permission govern retrieval or disclosure?
a: Engram has no epistemic permission dial; scope filters retrieval itself (internal/mcp/mcp.go:1123-1140).

q: What does the caller see on no match or partial failure?
a: mem_search returns a successful “No memories found” response; database search errors become tool errors suggesting simpler keywords; relation-annotation errors are silently ignored (internal/mcp/mcp.go:1141-1160).

q: Does old knowledge expire, disappear from retrieval, or merely require review?
a: Engram sets review dates at 3 months for preferences, 6 for decisions, and 12 for policies; other types never decay, and review state is virtual

q: What does delete mean?
a: Observations are soft-deleted by default; explicit hard delete exists, while session deletion is blocked if any observation—including soft-deleted—still references it (docs/codebase/memory-core.md:48; internal/store/store.go:3535-3582).

q: What ordering/idempotency is assumed?
a: MCP writes are serialized through one queue; started writes finish even if caller cancellation races, so outcome is deterministic (internal/mcp/write_queue.go:40-88).

q: What happens under local write contention?
a: SQLite busy/locked writes retry after 10, 25, and 50 ms, and MCP admits at most 32 queued writes (internal/store/store.go:42-51; internal/mcp/write_queue.go:12-35).
